shared_elements: human form (figures in A; carved anthropomorphic body in B)
curved bands or lines across a surface
low relief carving of motifs on a flat-ish field
justification: The only real correspondence is generic: both surfaces carry human-related forms and include circular disc motifs and curved band-like lines in low relief, features almost any tradition could produce. A depicts a legible ordered procession of profile figures in patterned robes carrying vessels above a register of rosettes, whereas B shows a few isolated, highly schematic swellings — a large ring, lumps and a curving belt-like band — spread over the rounded back of a massive body, with no narrative, no register lines and utterly different rendering conventions.
